req.title: Echo request headers
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET /headers with a JSON object whose 'headers' field mirrors the request headers received.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /headers must return a JSON object with a 'headers' field that mirrors the request headers. I designed tests covering: (1) positive EP — standard custom header is echoed exactly; (2) negative NEG — wrong HTTP method returns 405; (3) boundary BVA — empty custom header value is echoed; (4) DT — multiple custom headers all echoed; (5) EP — Host header always present in response; (6) BVA — single-character header value echoed exactly. Each test uses exact-value assertions to kill constant, operator, and boolean mutations.

tests.name: test_headers_echoes_custom_header_exactly
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send GET /headers with custom header X-Test-Header: hello-world
trace: R-HTTPBIN-012: system shall respond with JSON whose 'headers' field mirrors request headers
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_headers_echoes_custom_header_exactly():
    r = client.get('/headers', headers={'X-Test-Header': 'hello-world'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    assert 'headers' in data
    hdrs = data['headers']
    assert isinstance(hdrs, dict)
    assert hdrs['X-Test-Header'] == 'hello-world'

GET /headers endpoint mirrors headers without modification

tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_headers_header_value_not_mutated():
    expected_value = 'mutant-check-42'
    r = client.get('/headers', headers={'X-Exact-Value': expected_value})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    assert 'headers' in data
    hdrs = data['headers']
    assert hdrs['X-Exact-Value'] == expected_value
    assert hdrs['X-Exact-Value'] != 'mutant-check-43'
    assert hdrs['X-Exact-Value'] != 'mutant-check-41'
